_note: The traceability model of the case. Every ID used in the documents lives here. scripts/check-trace.mjs fails the build on an orphan: a pain nobody voiced, a goal without a KPI, a rule without an executable example, a story without a test, an ID in a document that does not exist. Fictional people and organisation.

quotes.text: At four o'clock I know three sailings are gone. At eleven I still don't know how many units that is, or which of them are reefers.
Six of us, a hundred and twenty calls, and every call is the same question. We rebook whoever gets through.
Last storm our biggest customer had forty trailers waiting until Saturday night, because they waited for their account manager — while a one-off customer who called at five sailed on Friday morning.
At cut-off I find nine reefers booked on a sailing with four free plugs. Then I'm the one bumping them.
Weather is weather. What I can't explain to the supermarket is that nobody told me my strawberries would sail on Saturday.
Every haulier still drives to the terminal, because nobody told them not to. At one in the morning trailers were parked on the access road.
My driver waited nineteen hours in his cab. He'd have stayed home if anyone had told him his new sailing.
Every storm someone books units that have no customs pre-lodgement. They take a slot, get refused at check-in, and the slot is gone.
Each storm the rules are reinvented by whoever is on duty. I want this to be boring.
We can't build 'be fair'. Give me rules a developer can test.
Fair is first come, first served. Anything else and my agents have to defend it on the phone.
Contract customers pay for capacity all year. In a storm they come first. Full stop.
Perishables and drivers first. The rest can wait a few hours — it won't rot.
Weather is force majeure. Show me a saving that isn't a claim we'd reject anyway.
quotes.parked: Not a pain: it shaped how the business case counts perishables (decision D-07).

quotes.text: The booking system knows lane metres. Plugs and ADR slots live in the load planner's spreadsheet.
Our commodity code in the booking? We type 'fresh' in the remarks. Sometimes.
If the system plans nine hundred units, I need to see why a unit is where it is. Otherwise I won't sign it.
Text the driver. Not an e-mail to our office that nobody reads at night.

pains.text: Nobody knows the size and shape of the backlog until the next morning.
The rebooking order is decided by who gets through on the phone, or who knows an account manager.
Plug, ADR and deck limits are discovered at cut-off: units are bumped late and space sails empty.
Perishables miss their deadline because nobody knows which reefers are perishable.
Hauliers and drivers come to a terminal that cannot load them: the yard overflows and drivers wait in their cabs.
The phone lines collapse; calls are abandoned and repeated.
Units without a customs pre-lodgement take recovery slots.
There is no agreed, explainable allocation policy; every storm is improvised.
Booking data cannot tell a perishable reefer from a frozen one.

goals.text: Certainty fast: 90% of stranded units have a confirmed new sailing within 2 hours of the cancellation decision.
Use the recovery capacity: no late bumps, and no lane metres sailing empty while usable units wait.
Protect what spoils: at least halve the perishables that sail after their deadline.
One agreed, explainable policy: every allocation carries a reason an agent can read out.
Keep the terminal flowing: the yard stays within capacity and drivers wait 40% less.
Customers get the answer before they call, and stay.

bat.title: Stranded-unit list is complete against the booking system
A reefer booking without commodity code is refused in the portal; EDI gets a warning
An agent explains three random allocations using only the why-panel
The duty manager reviews and approves a 900-unit plan within 30 minutes
Customer message: content, timing, one message per customer

decisions.title: Measure time to certainty, not rebooking speed
The system proposes, the duty manager decides
Plugs, ADR slots and deck height become sailing attributes in the booking platform
Commodity code and deliver-by time mandatory for reefer bookings
Add R-15 scarce slots first after the first simulation run
The business case counts goodwill paid, not claims rejected
Pilot before winter, with a storm drill as business acceptance
Driver texts use the booking contact; numbers kept 30 days
Reroute and pull-forward offers move to release 2
A smaller ship overrides stability: displaced confirmed units are re-planned and escalated (R-16)

risks.text: Booking data does not flag perishables, so the plan protects the wrong reefers.
The duty manager does not trust the plan and overrides everything.
Sales bypasses the plan for key accounts.
Customers ignore the message and call anyway.
Driver texts do not arrive because contact data is missing.
Plug and ADR data on sailings is wrong, so the plan cannot be loaded.
The first real storm arrives before go-live.
